method: full score_breakdown dump on search/hybrid and search (semantic-only)

key_findings.detail: Each search/hybrid result exposes: hybridScore, keywordScore, semanticScore, similarity (=hybridScore), score_breakdown{vector, bm25, hybrid}. Top-level also has metrics{search_tier, total_candidates, top_similarity, abstain_threshold}, weights{}, facets{}.

Records with higher importance_score and confidence_score (PiyAPI-assigned, not user metadata) are boosted in rank above records with higher hybridScore. Example: Atlas 'Acme Robotics' (hybridScore=0.731, imp=0.5, conf=0.65) ranked above Docker (hybridScore=0.821, imp=0.3, conf=0.3). In Q2, Atlas migration paraphrase (hybridScore=0.667, imp=0.55, conf=0.43) ranked above early meetings (hybridScore=0.825, imp=0.3, conf=0.3). The exact formula is opaque but importance_score and confidence_score clearly influence final rank order.

4 records appear in search results with version=0 and null confidence_score, but GET returns correct versions (v2-v3) and confidence scores. These records (PostgreSQL, SQLite, Podman, proj-atl in some queries) had their versions bumped by cross-record contradiction processing. The search index hasn't re-indexed them yet.

The v0/stale records show anomalously high hybridScores in some queries: PostgreSQL and SQLite scored 0.930 for 'Jamie Hart meetings' query (vs vec=0.738), and proj-atl scored 0.9295 (vs vec=0.656). These scores are impossibly high given their semantic relevance. Despite the high scores, these records are pushed to the END of results — PiyAPI appears to deprioritize unprocessed records regardless of score.

POST /search (semantic-only) returns results sorted correctly by similarity score in descending order. The sort anomaly is specific to search/hybrid, where the compound ranking includes importance/confidence boost.

alias.notes: Content-based matching: semantic search finds entity name in content text. All 14 alias queries found records about the canonical entity.

abstention.notes: PiyAPI always returns top-k results. No abstention capability. Queries about nonexistent facts (favorite color, shoe size, salary, founding date, false premise) all returned 10 results.

supersession.notes: Re-run after DNS recovery. All 6 supersession cases failed. System cannot distinguish current vs superseded records — no temporal ranking, no status-aware filtering.

dns_note: Initial run had DNS failures (nodename nor servname provided) on supersession and uncertainty categories. Re-ran those categories separately after API recovered. DNS failures were transient network issues, not API behavior.
